instruction:
Use FDIC guidance on insured deposits, ownership categories and excluded financial products. Compare single, joint and certain retirement accounts, stating aggregation rules, coverage limits and joint-account qualification requirements. Assess six independent examples in US dollars: A, one person's $180,000 checking and $120,000 savings at one bank; B, two people's $700,000 qualifying joint account with equal shares and no other joint accounts; C, one person's $180,000 traditional IRA deposit and $100,000 Roth IRA deposit at one bank; D, one person's $260,000 single deposit and $240,000 qualifying IRA deposit at one bank; E, one person's $220,000 single deposit at each of two separately chartered insured banks; F, one person's $200,000 single deposit and $50,000 mutual-fund holding purchased through the same bank. Unless specified otherwise, use one insured bank, no beneficiaries and no other balances. Assume the stated retirement accounts qualify and balances already include accrued interest. Show insured deposits, uninsured deposits and assets outside deposit-insurance coverage separately, with arithmetic and category-level citations. Explain why different branches, different ownership categories and separately chartered banks are not interchangeable.

Stopping condition: Stop when three category definitions, joint-account conditions, six cited balance calculations and the three aggregation distinctions are complete.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Evaluate if the agent defines the three specified ownership categories (Single Accounts, Joint Accounts, Certain Retirement Accounts) and states the standard insurance amount. Full credit if all three categories are defined and the $250,000 limit per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category is stated. Partial credit if 1-2 categories are defined or the general limit is omitted.

Evaluate if the agent explicitly states the FDIC requirements for a joint account to qualify for coverage (e.g., owned by two or more living people, equal rights to withdraw, all co-owners must have signed the deposit account signature card unless it's a CD). Full credit for accurately listing the FDIC qualification conditions. Partial credit for incomplete conditions.

Evaluate if the agent explains how accounts are aggregated and clearly distinguishes why different branches (deposits at branches of the same bank are combined), different ownership categories (separate limits apply to different categories), and separately chartered banks (each bank provides a separate $250k limit) are not interchangeable. Full credit if all three distinctions are clearly explained. Partial credit for missing 1-2 distinctions.

Evaluate the assessment of Example A ($180,000 checking + $120,000 savings). Full credit if the agent aggregates the balances under the Single Account category ($300,000 total) and correctly identifies $250,000 as insured and $50,000 as uninsured. Partial credit for minor arithmetic errors with correct logic.

Evaluate the assessment of Example B ($700,000 joint account, two people). Full credit if the agent calculates coverage for two co-owners under the Joint Account category ($250,000 x 2 = $500,000 insured) and correctly identifies $200,000 as uninsured. Partial credit for applying the wrong limit but showing the math.

Evaluate the assessment of Example C ($180,000 traditional IRA + $100,000 Roth IRA). Full credit if the agent aggregates the balances under the Certain Retirement Accounts category ($280,000 total) and correctly identifies $250,000 as insured and $30,000 as uninsured. Partial credit if accounts are incorrectly treated as separate categories but math is correct.

Evaluate the assessment of Example D ($260,000 single deposit + $240,000 qualifying IRA). Full credit if the agent treats them as separate categories, identifying Single ($250,000 insured, $10,000 uninsured) and Retirement ($240,000 insured, $0 uninsured). Partial credit if categories are wrongfully aggregated.

Evaluate the assessment of Example E ($220,000 single deposit at each of two separately chartered banks). Full credit if the agent applies separate limits for each bank, resulting in $440,000 total insured and $0 uninsured. Partial credit if incorrectly aggregated as if at the same bank.

Evaluate the assessment of Example F ($200,000 single deposit + $50,000 mutual-fund holding). Full credit if the agent identifies the $200,000 deposit as insured (Single category) and explicitly classifies the $50,000 mutual fund as an asset outside deposit-insurance coverage (not an uninsured deposit). Partial credit if the mutual fund is labeled as an uninsured deposit rather than an excluded asset.

Evaluate if the agent strictly follows the requested formatting: separating insured deposits, uninsured deposits, and assets outside coverage separately; showing arithmetic; and providing category-level citations for the calculations. Full credit if all formatting and citation constraints are met across the examples.
